mainTopic: The חכמים's reply to רבי יוחנן בן נורי about נבלת עוף טהור, and רבא on plans made while produce is attached and 'type' rules for מעשר
overview: The amud opens by explaining how the חכמים answered רבי יוחנן בן נורי. He used a קל וחומר to argue that the food-impurity of נבלת עוף טהור should not need מחשבה. The first explanation is that food-impurity spreads to similar items, but אביי shows this only makes the קל וחומר stronger. רב ששת then says the difference is הכשר. A משנה seems to say this carcass needs no הכשר, and the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל backs that up. Finally רבא, or some say רב פפא, explains that the חכמים compared whole categories of impurity. Next רבא says that for מעשר, even רבי יוחנן agrees that a plan made while produce is still attached counts. רב אשי rejects his proof from herbs in a courtyard and challenges him with the rule that whatever owes מעשר becomes impure as food. רבא answers that such rules speak about types (מין). A proof from a טרפה is pushed away by רבינא, but a ברייתא about an ownerless vineyard proves רבא right. The amud ends by quoting a משנה about פאה for dill or mustard sown in several spots, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First explanation of the חכמים's reply: one impurity spreads, the other does not
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים's reply is explained this way: the severe throat-impurity does not make something similar to itself impure, but food-impurity does. So you cannot learn one from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: You learned this about severe impurity, which does not make something like itself impure. Can you say the same about lenient impurity, which does make something like itself impure?
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of an explanation of how the חכמים answered רבי יוחנן בן נורי's קל וחומר. They point to a difference between the two kinds of impurity of a kosher bird's carcass.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The severe impurity (in the throat, it makes the person and his clothes impure) does not pass on to another person in the same way. Food-impurity does spread to other food. According to this explanation, that difference blocks the קל וחומר, so food-impurity might still need מחשבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Severe impurity: here, the special impurity of a kosher bird's carcass when it is in the throat
Lenient impurity: here, the carcass's impurity as ordinary food
Makes something similar to itself impure (passes on the same kind of impurity)
The carcass of a kosher bird that was not slaughtered properly

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two impurities. They both come from the same bird carcass. 'Severe' is the throat-impurity, and 'lenient' is the food-impurity.

phrases.english: [You said this] about severe impurity
phrases.notes: This is the throat-impurity: swallowing the carcass makes the person and his clothes impure.

phrases.english: since it does not make something like itself impure,
will you say the same about lenient impurity,
which does make something like itself impure?
phrases.notes: Impure food can make other food impure, even if only מדרבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּטוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה שֶׁכֵּן אֵינָהּ עוֹשָׂה כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the חכמים's rejection of רבי יוחנן בן נורי's קל וחומר, which began before this part of the text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קל וחומר is blocked because food-impurity spreads to similar items and the throat-impurity does not.

steps.title: אביי: that difference makes the argument stronger, not weaker
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that 'not spreading' is a leniency. So the throat-impurity is the weaker one in this respect. If even it works without מחשבה, food-impurity, which spreads, should all the more so work without מחשבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It's all the more so! The severe impurity is lenient in that it does not make something like itself impure, and yet it makes things impure without thought. The lenient impurity is strict in that it does make something like itself impure. Isn't it logical that it makes things impure without thought?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the first explanation. He shows that the difference it points to actually helps רבי יוחנן בן נורי's קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A refutation of a קל וחומר has to show that the source has some stricter feature that the target lacks. Here the feature named (not spreading) is a leniency of the source, and spreading is a stringency of the target. So the target is stricter on both counts, and the קל וחומר becomes a כל דכן, an even stronger argument.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so: the argument becomes even stronger
'Now if...': the opening of a קל וחומר
Intention: here, the intent to treat the carcass as food
Isn't it logical? The conclusion of a קל וחומר

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: כֹּל דְּכֵן הוּא,
phrases.english: אביי said to him: It is all the more so!
Now if the severe impurity, which is lenient [in one way],
in that it does not make something like itself impure,
still makes things impure without thought,
then the lenient impurity, which is strict [in one way],
in that it does make something like itself impure,
isn't it logical that it makes things impure without thought?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: כֹּל דְּכֵן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the חכמים rejected the קל וחומר because food-impurity spreads to similar items
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spreading is a stringency of the target, not of the source. So the difference strengthens the קל וחומר instead of blocking it.
steps.whatToRemember: To break a קל וחומר, you must find a stricter feature in the source case. Pointing to a leniency in the source only makes the argument stronger.

steps.title: רב ששת: the real difference is the need for הכשר
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains the חכמים's reply differently. The throat-impurity does not need הכשר (contact with liquid), but food-impurity does. Since food-impurity already needs one preparation step, it may need מחשבה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ששת said, this is what they meant: No, if you said this about severe impurity, which does not need הכשר, will you say it about lenient impurity, which does need הכשר?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first explanation failed, רב ששת offers a new explanation of the חכמים's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the difference named really is a stringency of the source: the throat-impurity works with no preparation at all. Food-impurity normally needs to be made wet first (הכשר). So it is reasonable that food-impurity also needs מחשבה, and the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier explanation and gives a new one
This is what he meant: a reinterpretation of a statement
Preparation: food must touch one of certain liquids before it can become impure
'No, if you said...': the standard way of rejecting a קל וחומר

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, הָכִי קָאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rather, רב ששת said: This is what they meant:
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים who answered רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

phrases.english: No! If you said [no thought is needed] for severe impurity,
that is because it does not need הכשר [contact with liquid];
will you say the same for lenient impurity,
which does need הכשר?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation in step 1, which אביי's challenge in step 2 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the חכמים's reply using a different distinguishing feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was that food-impurity spreads to similar items (step 1).
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is that food-impurity needs הכשר and the throat-impurity does not. This is a real stringency of the source, so it does block the קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the correct way to break a קל וחומר: name a feature that makes the source stricter.

steps.title: Challenge: a משנה says this carcass needs no הכשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the food-impurity of נבלת עוף טהור really needs הכשר. A משנה lists three rules for it: it needs מחשבה, it makes things impure only in the throat, and it does not need הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it really need הכשר? But we learned in a משנה: Three things were said about the carcass of a kosher bird: it needs thought, it makes impure only in the throat, and it does not need הכשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's explanation. A משנה says outright that this carcass does not need הכשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's whole distinction depends on food-impurity needing הכשר. The משנה says נבלת עוף טהור never needs הכשר, even for its food-impurity. If that is true, both impurities are the same on this point, and his explanation of the חכמים seems to collapse. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And does it really...?': opens a doubting question that leads into a challenge
The throat: where the carcass gives its severe impurity

phrases.english: But does it really need הכשר?
phrases.notes: He means the food-impurity of the kosher bird's carcass.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: Three things were said
about the carcass of a kosher bird:
it needs thought [to count as food],
it makes things impure only when in the throat,
and it does not need הכשר!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי צְרִיכָה הֶכְשֵׁר? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual basis of רב ששת's explanation in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the food-impurity of נבלת עוף טהור needs הכשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה states that נבלת עוף טהור does not need הכשר. That removes the difference רב ששת relied on.
steps.confusionAlert: The same משנה also says this carcass needs מחשבה. That fits the חכמים. The only problem raised here is the הכשר part.

steps.title: It needs water-preparation, just not creeping-animal preparation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's 'no הכשר' only means no הכשר שרץ. It still needs הכשר מים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, it does not need 'preparation by a creeping animal,' but it does need 'preparation by water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. It explains that the משנה was talking about only one kind of הכשר, not every kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 the משנה seemed to say that נבלת עוף טהור needs no הכשר at all, which would undo רב ששת's answer. The גמרא splits הכשר into two kinds: הכשר שרץ, which it does not need, and הכשר מים, which it does need. So רב ששת's point still stands: food-impurity needs a preparation step (water).

keyTerms.meaning: Preparation: something that makes a food able to become impure
The kind of preparation tied to a creeping animal. The bird's carcass does not need it, because its impurity is built in
Preparation by contact with water or another liquid
Granted, even if (it admits one point but holds onto another)

phrases.english: Granted that it does not need preparation by a creeping animal,
phrases.notes: So when the משנה said 'it does not need הכשר,' it meant only this kind.

phrases.english: it does need preparation by water.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּהֶכְשֵׁר שֶׁרֶץ לָא בָּעֲיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by narrowing what the משנה meant by 'no הכשר.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means the bird's carcass needs no הכשר of any kind, which would undo רב ששת.
steps.terutzMaskana: It needs no הכשר שרץ, but it does need הכשר מים, so רב ששת's reasoning survives.

steps.title: Why free it from one kind of preparation but not the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the split. The source that frees it from הכשר שרץ is the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל, and that same source should free it from הכשר מים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about creeping-animal preparation, that it is not needed? It is because of what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught. Then it should not need water-preparation either, because of what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 5. It asks why the same source should not cancel the need for water too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא points out that the reason the bird's carcass does not need הכשר שרץ comes from the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל. But that teaching is built on a פסוק about seeds and water. So if it frees the carcass from one kind of preparation, it should free it from הכשר מים as well. The split from step 5 seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks why two cases are treated differently)
It should not need

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא הֶכְשֵׁר שֶׁרֶץ דְּלָא בָּעֲיָא,
phrases.english: What is different about creeping-animal preparation, that it is not needed?
It is because of what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught?
Then water-preparation should also not be needed,
because of what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught!
phrases.notes: Same source both times. That is the whole point of the question.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הֶכְשֵׁר שֶׁרֶץ דְּלָא בָּעֲיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the split between הכשר שרץ and הכשר מים made in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that the bird's carcass still needs הכשר מים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל is the source for not needing הכשר. It is based on a פסוק about seeds and water, so it should cancel the need for water too.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל: only things that never carry severe impurity need preparation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the teaching from the פסוק about seeds. Like seeds, anything that will never carry severe impurity needs הכשר. נבלת עוף טהור, which will carry severe impurity, does not need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'Upon any sowing seed that is to be sown.' Seeds will never make things impure with severe impurity, and they need preparation. So too, anything that will never make things impure with severe impurity needs preparation. This leaves out the carcass of a kosher bird, which will make things impure with severe impurity, so it does not need preparation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the source it mentioned in step 6. This shows why that source should cover water-preparation too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about seeds teaches that food needs contact with water before it can become impure. The school of רבי ישמעאל compares other items to seeds: only things that, like seeds, will never carry severe impurity need this preparation. Since נבלת עוף טהור will one day carry severe impurity (in the throat), it is left out. The preparation it is left out of is the water-preparation from this very פסוק, which backs up the challenge in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Seeds, standing for ordinary foods
Severe impurity, the kind that can make a person or clothing impure
That will never in the end (do something)
Just as... so too (comparing other cases to the one in the פסוק)
This leaves out (an exception to the rule)
The carcass of a kosher bird that was not properly slaughtered

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of the school of רבי ישמעאל ties the need for הכשר to things that never carry severe impurity. נבלת עוף טהור does carry severe impurity in the throat, so this teaching frees it from the water-preparation of the פסוק itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This source comes straight from the פסוק about water on seeds. So it seriously threatens the attempt in step 5 to say the bird's carcass still needs הכשר מים.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Upon any sowing seed that is to be sown."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:37–38. The next פסוק says seeds become impure only after water is put on them.

phrases.english: Just as seeds, which will never in the end
make things impure with severe impurity, need preparation,
so too, anything that will never in the end
make things impure with severe impurity needs preparation.
This leaves out the carcass of a kosher bird,
which will in the end make things impure with severe impurity,
phrases.notes: This means when it is in a person's throat, the case from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: so it does not need preparation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the source used in the challenge of step 6, to back it up.
steps.raayaObject: That the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל frees נבלת עוף טהור from water-preparation too.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל on ויקרא 11:37–38, comparing items to seeds.

steps.title: The חכמים look at whole categories of impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or some say רב פפא, gives a new answer. The חכמים mean the category as a whole: severe impurity in general never needs הכשר, while lenient food impurity in general does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, and some say רב פפא: think of severe impurity as a whole category, and lenient impurity as a whole category.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier answer broke down, so the גמרא drops it with אלא and gives a new explanation of the חכמים's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw that נבלת עוף טהור does not need הכשר at all, so we cannot say its food impurity needs one step of preparation. The new answer says the חכמים judge by the category. Severe impurity in general never needs הכשר. Lenient food impurity in general does need it, so it can also need מחשבה, even if נבלת עוף טהור is an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Name, meaning the general category
Severe impurity, here the impurity of the throat
Lenient impurity, here ordinary food impurity
In general, across the whole category

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים compare categories, not single cases. Lenient food impurity as a category needs הכשר, so it can need מחשבה too, even for נבלת עוף טהור.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say נבלת עוף טהור needs הכשר. It doesn't. It is an exception inside a category that usually does.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said,
and some say it was Rav Pappa:
the category of severe impurity in general,
phrases.notes: He means: no severe impurity anywhere needs contact with liquid.

phrases.english: the category of lenient impurity in general.
phrases.notes: Food impurity as a group usually does need liquid, so it can also need מחשבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of רב ששת after steps 6-7 showed that נבלת עוף טהור needs no הכשר at all
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: compare general categories instead of the single case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים's reply depends on whether the food impurity of נבלת עוף טהור itself needs הכשר
steps.terutzMaskana: The reply depends on the categories as a whole: severe impurity never needs הכשר, while lenient food impurity generally does

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees that a plan made while attached counts for מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that for מעשר, רבי יוחנן agrees that a plan made while the produce is still attached to the ground counts as a real plan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יוחנן agrees, when it comes to מעשר, that a plan made while the produce is attached counts as a plan.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new topic. He limits רבי יוחנן's view that a plan made while produce is attached does not count, and says it does count for מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'agrees' tells us that רבי יוחנן usually holds that such a plan does not count. רבא says that for מעשר he admits it does count. So if someone decides while the plant is still growing to use it as food, that decision can create an obligation to tithe.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, admits on this point
The tithe taken from produce
A plan made while the produce is still attached to the ground
Counts as a real plan

phrases.english: Rava said:
And Rabbi Yoḥanan agrees with regard to tithes,
that a plan made while attached counts as a plan.
phrases.notes: Attached means the produce is still growing in the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְעִנְיַן מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the impurity discussion and opens a new point about רבי יוחנן and מעשר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מעשר, a plan made while produce is still attached to the ground counts as a plan, even according to רבי יוחנן

steps.title: רבא brings a משנה about herbs in a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה: certain herbs growing in a courtyard must be tithed if they were guarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? Because we learned in a משנה: savory, hyssop, and thyme growing in a courtyard, if they were guarded, must be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his proof by quoting a משנה. The next step will explain how this משנה proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These herbs are not always grown as human food. The משנה says that if they were guarded, the owner must tithe them. רבא will show that this fits only if a plan made while they were attached counted.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I know this? The opening of a proof
Savory, hyssop and thyme, kinds of hyssop-like herbs
Guarded, protected by the owner
Obligated, here to take מעשר

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this?
As we learned in a mishna:
Savory, hyssop, and thyme that are in a courtyard,
if they were guarded, they are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבא's statement in step 9
steps.raayaObject: That a plan made while attached counts for מעשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה מעשרות 3:9 about herbs in a courtyard

steps.title: The משנה must mean herbs first planted for animals
steps.stepSummary: If the herbs were planted for people, the ruling would be obvious. So the משנה must mean herbs planted for animals that the owner later decided to use as human food while they were still growing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say they were planted for people from the start, does it need to be said? Rather, they must have been planted for animals from the start, and still the משנה teaches: if they were guarded, they must be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the משנה proves רבא's point. It asks what case the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Herbs planted for people and guarded obviously need tithing, so the משנה would not bother to say it. It must be about herbs planted for animals, which became human food only through the owner's later plan, made while they were still attached. Since the משנה requires tithing, that plan counted.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?
Does it need to be said? It is obvious
Rather, is it not that, the only remaining option

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that he planted them from the start for people,
does it need to be said?
Rather, is it not that he planted them from the start for animals,
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes he later changed his mind and planned to eat them while they were still growing.

phrases.english: and it teaches: If they were guarded, they are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּזַרְעִינְהוּ מִתְּחִלָּה לָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the משנה from step 10 proves רבא's claim
steps.raayaObject: That the owner's plan made while the herbs were attached turned them into food that must be tithed
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading of the משנה: the planted-for-people case would be obvious, so it must be the planted-for-animals case

steps.title: רב אשי: the herbs grew by themselves
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof. The משנה is about herbs that grew by themselves, which count as human food by default. Its real point is whether the courtyard guards its produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Here we are dealing with a courtyard where the herbs grew by themselves, and herbs like that are meant for people by default. The משנה means: if the courtyard guards its produce, they must be tithed, and if not, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes away רבא's proof. He shows the משנה can be read without any plan made while the herbs were attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא thought the only new case was herbs planted for animals. רב אשי offers a third case: herbs that grew wild. With no one planting them, they count as human food by default, so no plan is needed. The משנה is only teaching about guarding: a courtyard that guards its produce makes them obligated, and one that doesn't leaves them exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Grew by themselves, without being planted
By default, when no one decided anything
This is what it means, a new reading of the text
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's reading removes the proof. The משנה is about wild herbs, which are human food by default, and about guarding. It says nothing about a plan made while attached.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Guarded' here means the courtyard protects what grows in it. It is not about what the owner planned.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Here we are dealing with a courtyard where they grew by themselves,
and by default they stand for people,
and this is what it is saying:
if the courtyard guards its produce, they are obligated,
and if not, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָכָא בְּחָצֵר שֶׁעָלוּ מֵאֵילֵיהֶן עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 10-11 by offering a different case for the משנה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not necessarily רבא's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא missed a third case, herbs that grew by themselves, which are human food by default without any plan

steps.title: A משנה seems to contradict רבא's distinction
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes a משנה saying whatever owes מעשר becomes impure as food. Under רבא's view, the replanned herbs would owe מעשר without becoming impure, which breaks that rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: the משנה says, 'Anything that must be tithed can become impure as food.' But if רבא is right, there are herbs that must be tithed and still cannot become impure as food!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רבא's statement that a plan made while the produce is still attached counts for מעשר. He brings a משנה that seems to say otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבא, herbs planted for animals and then set aside for people while still growing would owe מעשר. For טומאה, though, רבי יוחנן says a plan made while the produce is attached does not count, so these herbs would not become impure as food. That would be a case of 'owes מעשר but no food impurity,' and the משנה says such a case cannot exist.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithes, the portions taken from produce
The ritual impurity that applies to food
'And if it is so', meaning if your view is correct

phrases.english: Rav Ashi raises an objection:
"Anything that is obligated in tithes
becomes impure with the impurity of food."
But if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבא is right that a plan made while the produce is still attached counts for מעשר.

phrases.english: there are these (herbs)
phrases.notes: He means produce first planted for animals, then set aside for people while still growing, like the case in step 11.

phrases.english: that are obligated in tithe
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: but do not become impure with the impurity of food!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even though רב אשי turned down רבא's proof in Step 12, he now goes further and challenges רבא's position directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that a plan made while the produce is attached counts for מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's view creates produce that owes מעשר but cannot become impure as food. The משנה says everything that owes מעשר can become impure as food.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about types of food
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה means any type of food that owes מעשר can become impure as food. It is not a promise about every single case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this is what the משנה means. Any type of food that must be tithed can become impure as food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his view by reading the משנה more narrowly. It speaks about kinds of food, not every situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Herbs as a kind owe מעשר and can become impure as food, so the משנה's rule holds. A special case, like herbs whose plan was made while still attached, can be an exception without breaking the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means', used to explain the true sense of a text
Type or kind

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying these herbs stop being food. Herbs are still a type of food that owes מעשר. This one case just has an unusual result for טומאה.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what it is saying —
any type that is obligated in tithe
becomes impure with the impurity of food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה as a rule about categories
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה covers every individual case of produce that owes מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks about types of food. Individual cases can be exceptions.

steps.title: Support from the next part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבא's reading by quoting the later part of the same משנה about ראשית הגז and the מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, because the end of the משנה teaches: whatever owes the first shearing also owes the gifts, but some animals owe the gifts and not the first shearing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof for רבא by quoting the end of the same משנה. This step sets up the source, and the next step shows how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part of the משנה states a broad 'whatever has X has Y' rule about animals. If that rule turns out to have an exception, it must be about types, and the same would then be true of the מעשר rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This also makes sense', which introduces support for the last answer
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
The first shearing of wool, given to a כהן
The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: foreleg, jaw, and maw

phrases.english: This too stands to reason,
since the last part teaches:
Anything obligated in the first shearing
is obligated in the gifts,
and there is that which is obligated in the gifts
but is not obligated in the first shearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to back up רבא's answer in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading that the משנה's rules are about types
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the same משנה, about ראשית הגז and the מתנות

steps.title: The טרפה shows the rule is about types
steps.stepSummary: A טרפה owes ראשית הגז but not the מתנות. So the משנה's rule cannot cover every case, which proves it speaks about types.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the rule covered every case, there would be a problem: a טרפה owes the first shearing but does not owe the gifts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It points to a case that breaks the משנה's rule if the rule is read as covering every single animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sheep that is a טרפה still owes ראשית הגז, but since it may not be eaten, the מתנות do not apply. The משנה could not have missed this, so it must mean types of animals. That supports reading the מעשר rule as being about types too, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
'But there is', which points to a case that seems to break a rule

steps.whatToRemember: This proof tries to show that the rules in this משנה ('whatever has X has Y') speak about general types, not every case. But watch the next step: רבינא pushes this proof away, and רבא's reading is only proven later, in step 19, from the ownerless vineyard.
steps.whyThisMatters: Reading a rule as being about types lets a single unusual case stand without breaking the general rule.

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the משנה's rule really covered every single case.

phrases.english: there is the case of a tereifa,
which is obligated in the first shearing
but is not obligated in the gifts!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, הָאִיכָּא טְרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof that Step 15 set up.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading that the משנה's rules are about types
steps.raayaSupportSource: The טרפה, which owes ראשית הגז but not the מתנות

steps.title: רבינא: The משנה Follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rejects the טרפה proof. The משנה may follow רבי שמעון, who exempts a טרפה from ראשית הגז, so the rule could still cover every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי שמעון's. We learned that רבי שמעון exempts a טרפה from the first shearing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא knocks down the proof from step 16. He says the משנה follows רבי שמעון, and for him the טרפה is not an exception at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 16 needed a טרפה to owe ראשית הגז but not the מתנות. According to רבי שמעון, a טרפה owes neither one. So the משנה could still be a rule about every single case, and the proof for רבא falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? The גמרא is asking which תנא the source follows.
An animal with a fatal defect
The first shearing of wool, given to a כהן
Exempts

phrases.english: Ravina said: Whose view is this?
phrases.notes: He means the משנה quoted in step 15 about ראשית הגז and the מתנות.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon's,
as we learned: Rabbi Shimon exempts
the tereifa from the first shearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבינא: הא מני? רבי שמעון היא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from steps 15 and 16 by naming the תנא of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from טרפה only. רבא's reading is not disproven, it is just left without that proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a טרפה owes ראשית הגז. רבי שמעון exempts it, so it is no exception to the rule.

steps.title: The Ownerless Vineyard Owes פאה but Not מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי brings a source: a man who made his vineyard ownerless and then harvested it the next morning owes the gifts for the poor, including פאה, but is exempt from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: Come and hear. If someone declares his vineyard ownerless, then gets up early in the morning and harvests it, he must still give פרט, עוללות, שכחה and פאה, but he is exempt from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי brings a new source to help רבא. It shows a case that owes פאה but does not owe מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ownerless produce is exempt from מעשר. But the gifts for the poor still apply to this harvest. So here פאה is owed without מעשר, and the next step will use this against reading the משנה as covering every single case.

keyTerms.meaning: One who declares his property ownerless (הפקר)
Single grapes that fall during the harvest, left for the poor
Small, incomplete grape clusters, left for the poor
Produce forgotten in the field, left for the poor
The corner of the field, left for the poor
The tithe taken from produce

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said: Come and hear:
One who declares his vineyard ownerless,
and rose early in the morning and harvested it,
is obligated in fallen grapes and in incomplete clusters,
and in forgotten clusters, and in pe'ah,
and is exempt from the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב שימי בר אשי, תא שמע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבינא rejected the טרפה proof, a new and stronger proof for רבא is brought.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading that the משנה speaks about types, not every case
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a vineyard made ownerless and then harvested by its owner

steps.title: So the משנה Speaks About Types
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says whatever owes פאה owes מעשר, yet the ownerless vineyard owes פאה without מעשר. So the משנה must speak about types of produce, just as רבא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: whatever owes פאה owes מעשר! Must we not learn from this that the משנה is speaking about types? Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from step 18. It concludes that רבא is right: these rules speak about types of produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'whatever owes פאה owes מעשר' meant every single case, the ownerless vineyard would break it. Since the ברייתא clearly says this vineyard owes פאה but not מעשר, the rule must mean that any type of produce that owes פאה is also a type that owes מעשר. The same reading fits the rule about food impurity, which supports רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is teaching about types (kinds of produce), not every single case
Rather, is it not that... (introduces the forced conclusion)
Learn from it; the point is proven
Tithes

steps.whatToRemember: Rules like 'whatever owes פאה owes מעשר' are about types of produce (מין). A single case, like an ownerless vineyard, can be an exception. This supports רבא.
steps.confusionAlert: The ownerless vineyard does not show that grapes are not a type that owes מעשר. Grapes are still that type. This case is just an exception because the vineyard was ownerless.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
whatever is obligated in pe'ah
is obligated in tithes!
Rather, must we not learn from it:
it teaches about types. Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא לאו שמע מינה: מין קתני, שמע מינה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof begun in step 18 and draws the conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's rules speak about types of produce (מין), as רבא said, so single exceptions are allowed.

steps.title: Dill or Mustard Sown in Several Spots Needs פאה From Each
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another משנה: the חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא that someone who sows dill or mustard in two or three spots gives פאה from each spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned elsewhere: the חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא that if someone sows dill or mustard in two or three places, he gives פאה from each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about פאה by quoting a משנה from another place. It is setting up the next move, which will come in the following lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue about whether separate patches in one field need separate פאה. Here, for dill and mustard, even the חכמים agree that each spot needs its own פאה. The גמרא quotes this now so it can discuss it next.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים agree (even though they argue elsewhere)
Dill
Mustard
From each and every one

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה from מסכת פאה.

phrases.english: The Sages agree with Rabbi Akiva
about one who sows dill or mustard
in two or three places,
that he gives pe'ah from each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנן התם: מודים חכמים לרבי עקיבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about פאה after the previous topic ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dill or mustard sown in two or three separate spots needs פאה from each spot, and even the חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא here.
